key_insight: Interval-aware AI models predicted subsolid pulmonary nodule growth and future morphology from baseline CT across follow-up periods ranging from months to years.
clinical_relevance: Time-aware predictions may support individualized nodule surveillance, but clinical benefit remains to be established.
method: Retrospective, single-center study of longitudinal CT scans.
Discriminative model used baseline CT, segmentation masks, and interscan intervals to predict growth.
Temporally conditioned generative model predicted future lesion morphology.
evidence_signal: Across 24,946 scan pairings from 2,543 nodules in 426 patients, test growth prediction achieved an AUROC of 0.772 (95% CI: 0.704–0.818), 80.2% sensitivity, and 58.7% specificity; morphology prediction achieved Dice 0.706 ± 0.186.
watch_item: Performance declined at longer follow-up intervals, and the single-center retrospective findings require external validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Prediction of Subsolid Pulmonary Nodule Evolution from Baseline CT Using Temporal Imaging Models
